la:verb:insequor.gloss: to follow, follow after or upon someone or something; pursue, follow up, press upon; attack, chase
senses: to follow, follow after or upon someone or something; pursue, follow up, press upon; attack, chase
la:verb:insequor.html:
in-sĕquor, cūtus (quūtus), 3,
v. dep. n. and a., to follow, to follow after or upon a person or thing (class.).
Lit.
In gen.: proximus huic, longo sed proximus intervallo Insequitur Salius,: fugientem lumine pinum,with her eyes follows the flying ship,.—
In partic., to pursue, follow up, press upon:

gens eadem quae te bello Insequitur, : hostem,; ; : ad hostem insequendum,: reliquias Troiae cineres atque ossa peremptae,: aliquem gladio stricto,; so ; fin. al.—

Of time, to follow, succeed (in verb. fin. rare; cf. P. a. infra): hunc proximo saeculo Themistocles insecutus est,; .—
Trop.
In gen.: improborum facta suspicie insequitur,. —
In partic.
To strive after, endeavor: nec vero te rhetoricis quibusdam libris insequor, ut erudiam,.—
To proceed: pergam atque insequar longius,.—Poet. with inf.: rursus et alterius lentum convellere vimen Insequor,.—
To overtake: at mors insecuta est Gracchum,. —
To pursue in a hostile manner with words, to censure, reproach, etc.: homines benevolos contumeliā,: irridendo,: clamore ac minis,: turpitudinem vitae,: dissimiles,.—
Of order or succession, to follow, come next: postremam litteram detrahebant, nisi vocalis insequebatur,: praesagium insequentis casus,.—Hence, insĕquens, entis, P. a., of time, following: annus,; : diei insequentis pars,: nocte insequenti,: anno,: tempore,: insequentium aetatum principes,.—
Of logical order: ex prioribus geometria probat insequentia,; cf. — * Adv.: insĕquenter, i. q. protinus, deinceps, thereupon, immediately, .

insanus
, to be of unsound mind (syn.: furo, deliro, desipio).

To be senseless, without reason, mad, insane: insanire ex amore,: homo insanibat (for insaniebat),: usque eo est commotus, ut insanire omnibus ac furere videretur,: insanire tibi videris, quod, etc.,: nisi ego insanio,: ex injuria,; : cum ratione,: certa ratione modoque,. —

Insanivisti hercle,: amavi equidem olim in adulescentia: Verum ad hoc exemplum numquam ut nunc insanio,: insanire libet quoniam tibi,: manu,i. e. in battle,.— Of speech; dicendi genus. quod ... specie libertatis insanit,.—Of a rage for building, .—
With acc.: errorem. : sollemnia,,

1, 101: amores alicujus,to be madly in love with one, (3, 32, 25 M.): hilarem insaniam insanire,. —

la:verb:instituo.gloss: to set up, establish, found, institute or arrange
senses: to set up, establish, found, institute or arrange
to train, teach, instruct, educate (usually by a course of training)
to make (something) a habit, practice, or custom
to appoint (typically, a guardian or heir)
to begin, undertake, purpose, determine (typically, some purpose, plan or project)
la:verb:instituo.html:
instĭtŭo, ŭi, ūtum (institivi, ), 3, v. a.
in-statuo
.
To put or place into, to plant, fix, set (cf.: instruo, informo; class.): vestigia nuda sinistri Instituere pedis,.— Trop.: argumenta in pectus multa institui, I have put, i. e. formed in my heart, : quemquamne hominem in animum instituere, aut parare, i. e. to set his heart on (al. in animo), .—
To set up, erect, plant, establish, arrange: vestigia,: arborem,: pratum,: jugera tercenta, ubi institui vineae possunt,: portorium vini,to lay on, impose,: instituit officinam Syracusis in regia maximam,founded, erected,: mercatum,: codicem et conscribere,: bibliothecam,. —
In gen., to make, fabricate, construct: magnus muralium pilorum numerus instituitur,: naves,to build,: pontem,to construct,: turres,: amphora coepit institui,: convivia,: longiorem sermonem,to hold,: delectum,: remiges ex provincia,to obtain, procure,.—
To prepare, furnish, provide (viands, food, a feast, etc.): dapes,: convivium,: convivia jucunda,.—
Trop.
To institute, found, establish, organize, set up (of institutions, governments, etc.); cf.: ibi regnum magnum institutum,: quo in magistratu non institutum est a me regnum, sed repressum,: so, magistratum,: de civitatibus instituendis littera,: civitatis formam,: is id regnum cum fratribus suis instituit,: ab instituta gente,: collegium figulorum,: aerarium militare,: stipendia,.—So of holidays, games, etc.: ferias diesque festos,: Saturnalia institutus festus dies,: sacros ludos,.—
To institute, appoint one, esp. as heir or to an office: qui me cum tutorem, tum etiam secundum heredem instituerit,: Populum Romanum tutorem,: magistratum,; ; ; ; ; .—
With ut, to ordain that: Arcesilas instituit, ut ii, qui, etc., Cic. Fin. 2, 1, 2: ut fierent quaestores),; .—With the simple subj.: instituit, quotannis subsortitio a praetore fieret,.—
To take upon one's self, to undertake: ubi cenas hodie, si hanc rationem instituis?: cum Zenone Arcesilas sibi omne certamen instituit,.—
To undertake, begin, commence: id negotium institutum est,: si diligentiam, quam instituisti, adhibueris,: perge tenere istam viam, quam instituisti,: ad hunc ipsum quaedam institui,: historia nec institui potest sine, etc.,: iter,.— With inf.: ut primum Velia navigare coepi, institui Topica conscribere,: flagitare,: si quae non nupta mulier virorum alienissimorum conviviis uti instituerit,begun, made it a practice,: recitare omnia,. —
Of troops, to draw up, arrange: tu actionem instituis, ille aciem instruit,: quartae aciei quam instituerat, signum dedit,.—
To provide, procure: quaestum,: aliquos sibi amicos,: animum ad cogitandum,apply,. —
To purpose, determine, resolve upon: in praesentia (Caesar) similem rationem operis instituit,. —With inf.: senex scribere historias instituit,: quaerere tempus ejus interficiendi,: montanos oppugnare,: habere secum,: coronas ad ipsum mittere,.— With object-clause: frumentum plebi dari,.—
To order, govern, administer, regulate: sapienter vitam instituit,: libri de civitatibus instituendis,: mores,: familiam,.—
To teach, instruct, train up, educate: sic tu instituis adulescentes?: oratorem, Quint.1, 1, 21.—With inf.: Latine loqui,: Pan primus calamos cerā conjungere plures Instituit,; ; : amphora fumum bibere instituta Consule Tullo,: cum tibiis canere voce instituit,.—With abl.: aliquem disciplinis Graecis,: lyrā,: disciplina Romana,.—With ad: aliquem ad dicendum,: aliquem artibus et moribus,: filios instituere atque erudire ad majorum instituta,; : ad lectionem,.— With ut or ne and subj.: quem tu a puero sic instituisses, ut nobili ne gladiatori quidem faveret,: pueros, ut, etc.,; : nos, ne quem coleremus, etc.,.—Of animals: boves,

inspĭcĭo, spexi, spectum, 3, v. a.
inspecio
,
to look into; to look at, inspect; to consider, contemplate, examine (class.).
Lit.
In gen.: intro inspice,: inspicere tanquam in speculum, in vitas omnium,: cum Romam inspexerit Eos,: inspice quid portem,: faciem,: ranarum viscera,: ea est procul inspicientibus natura loci, ut,: libros,: leges,: aurum inspicere, ne subruptum siet,to examine whether,.—

la:noun:instrumentum.html:
instrūmentum, i, n.
id.
,
an implement of any kind, a utensil, tool, instrument (class.).
Lit.: militare,: culinarum argentea,: crudelia jussae instrumenta necis,.—
Esp., sing. collect., instruments, apparatus, material, stock, furniture (freq. and class.): instrumentum ac ornamenta villae,: orationes magna impensā magnoque instrumento tueri,: belli instrumentum et apparatus,: rusticum, ; : hostium spolia, monumenta imperatorum, decora atque ornamenta fanorum, in instrumento atque in supellectile Verris nominabuntur,; cf. : hibernorum,: bellicum,: nauticum,: venatorium,: piscationis,.—Esp., in law, the personalty, chattels, or stock of a farm, business, trade, etc.: fundo legato, neque instrumentum fundi ... ad legatarium pertinet,: instrumento cauponio legato, ea debentur, quae in cauponis usum parata sunt, velut vasa,: pistoris, § 64: medici,; cf.: in fanis alia vasorum sunt et sacrae supellectilis, alia ornamentorum, quae vasorum sunt instrumenti instar habent, quibus sacrificia conficiuntur,apparatus,. —

insĭdĭae, ārum, f.plur. (in sing. insidia prima, ap. P.) [insideo],
an ambush, ambuscade (class.).
Lit
Of persons: qui sustinuerant primos impetus insidiarum,: equites procedere longius jussi, donec insidiae coorirentur,.—
Of place: si forte in insidias devenero,: signa aenea in insidiis ponere,: milites in insidiis collocare,: intrare insidias,.—Particular phrases.
To lay an ambush for any one: insidias dare alicui,: facere vitae alicujus,: ponere vitae alicujus,: insidias penitus abstrusas ponere contra aliquem,: parare alicui,: tendere,: collocare,: comparare,: struere,: componere,: compo nere in aliquem, (3, 30), 19: componere

la:verb:insto.gloss: to stand upon, set foot on
senses: to stand upon, set foot on
to be nearby, close to, be imminent
to urge, pursue, insist, to be intent upon
to be pressing, draw nigh, approach, threaten
la:verb:insto.html:
in-sto, stĭti, stātum (e. g. instaturum, :
instaturos,), 1, v. n., to stand in or upon a thing (class.).
Lit.
In gen., constr. with dat., in and abl., or acc.
With dat.: jugis,.—
With in and abl.: saxo in globoso, Pac. ap. (Trag. Fragm. v. 367 Rib.): instans in medio triclinio,.—
Absol., to draw nigh, approach; to impend, threaten: quibus ego confido impendere fatum aliquod, et poenas jam diu debitas aut instare jam plane, aut certe jam appropinquare,: instant apparatissimi magnificentissimique ludi,: cum illi iter instaret,: quidquid subiti et magni discriminis instat,: ante factis omissis, illud quod instet, agi oportere,the subject in hand,. — Of persons: cum legionibus instare Varum,.—
With acc. (ante-class.): tantum eum instat exitii,.—
In partic., to press upon, harass, molest, menace, threaten.—With dat., acc., or absol.
With dat.: cedenti,: vestigiis,: instantem regi cometen videre,.—
With acc.: si me instabunt (al. mi),.—
Trop.
To urge or press upon one, to insist; to pursue a thing (syn. urgeo): quamobrem urge, insta, perfice,: accusatori,: ille instat factum (esse),he insists upon the fact,.—To follow up eagerly, pursue; with dat. or acc.
With dat.: instant operi regnisque futuris,: talibus instans monitis (parens),: non ignarus instandum famae,.—
With acc., to urge forward, ply, transact with zeal or diligence: instant mercaturam, Nov. ap. (Com. Rel. p. 223 Rib.): parte aliā Marti currumque, rotasque volucres Instabant,were hastening forward, working hard at, busily constructing,: rectam viam, to go right, i. e. to be right, to hit the mark, : unum instare de indutiis vehementissime contendere,; cf. Zumpt, Gram. § 385.—
Absol.: vox domini instantis,.—
To demand earnestly, solicit, insist upon: satis est, quod instat de Milone,: quod profecto cum sua sponte, tum, te instante, faciet,at your instance, your solicitation,.— With inf.: instat Scandilius poscere recuperatores,.—With ut or ne: tibi instat Hortensius, ut eas in consilium,: uxor acriter tua instat, ne mihi detur,; cf.: nunc nosmet ipsi nobis instemus, ut, etc.,.—Impers.: profecto, si instetur, suo milite vinci Romam posse,.—Hence, instans, antis, P. a.
(Standing by, being near, i. e.) Present.
In gen.: quae venientia metuuntur, eadem efficiunt aegritudinem instantia,: ex controversia futuri, raro etiam ex instantis aut facti,: tempus,: bellum,.—
In partic., gram. t. t.: tempus, i.q. praesens tempus,the present tense, the present,; P. et saep.—
Pressing, urgent, importunate (post-Aug.): periculum,: species terribilior jam et instantior,: gestus acer atque instans,; cf.: argumentatio acrior et instantior,: admonitio instantior,.—Adv.: instanter, vehemently, earnestly, pressingly: intente instanterque pronuntiare,: petere,: plura acriter et instanter incipere,: dicere,.— Comp.: instantius concurrere,to fight more vehemently,. — Sup.: instantissime desiderare,.

Esp., with se, to wind one's way into, to steal into; to insinuate or ingratiate one's self: se inter equitum turmas,: quā te insinuaveris, retro via repetenda,: cum (Romanus) insinuasset se inter corpus armaque,: qua se inter valles flumen insinuat,winds along,: Tigris Persico mari se insinuat,.—

In gen.: Augusto insinuatus est,; ; : hoc est quod penitus illos animo Caesaris insinuavit,; cf.: vitam moresque feris mentibus,.—
Esp., reflex. with se, etc.
With ad or in and acc.: his nos rebus insinuabimus ad causam,will make our way to, get to,: se in antiquam philosophiam,: se ad aliquam,: se in familiaritatem alicujus,: se in amicitiam cum aliquo,; : se in forum,: se in familiarem usum,: se in eorum sermonem,.—
Absol.: callidus ille ne se insinuet, studiose cavendum est,: eadem qua te insinuaveris via retro repetenda est,: celeriter dato loco cum se insinuasset, Auct. B. Alex. 52, 2: praefecto regis se,: plebi se,.—
To introduce to, initiate into: adest tibi dies, quo per istas meas manus piissimis sacrorum arcanis insinueris,.—
To make known, publish (post-class.): voluntatem suam heredibus,; .—
Neutr., to wind or steal into, to make one's way or get into, to penetrate, enter, reach, arrive at; constr. with in and acc. or dat.: inde in amicitiam insinuavit cum matre et mecum simul. Blanditiis, etc., : penitus insinuare in causam,to penetrate thoroughly into, to acquire a complete knowledge of,; cf.: ad causam,: in ipsius consuetudinem insinuabo,: novus per pectora cunctis Insinuat pavor,: Italiaeque urbes dextram insinuantis in undam,winding, reaching to,: et blandiri suppliciter et subtiliter insinuare eis, a quibus, etc., i. e. to steal into favor with, etc., .
la:verb:insinuo.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.

la:noun:insolentia.html:
in-sŏlentĭa, ae, f.
insolens
.

In gen.: fori, judiciorumque,: itineris,: loci,: voluptatum,: disputationis,.—
Rhet., unusualness, novelty, strangeness, affectedness in the choice of words: orationis,: verborum,: peregrina,.—In plur.: insolentias verborum a veteribus dictorum respuere,.—
Want of moderation, pride, haughtiness, arrogance, insolence: illa tua singularis insolentia, superbia, contumacia,; , § 106; lavish indulgence; opp. continentiam, ; : hominis,: modeste insolentiam suam continere,: ex secundis rebus,: insolentiam alicui obicere,: gloriae,. — Plur.: spiritus a noxiorum insolentiis premitur,, epil. 31.

in-sŏlens, ntis, adj.

Excessive, immoderate; haughty, arrogant, insolent: insolenti alacritate gestire,: ostentatio,: victoria,: laetitia,: exercitus,: nec erat ei verendum, ne vera de se praedicans, nimis videretur aut insolens, aut loquax,: ne in re nota multus et insolens sim,: non tam insolens sum, quam ineruditus,: nihil umquam neque insolens, neque gloriosum ex ore ejus exiit,: Fortuna ludum insolentem ludere pertinax,.— Comp.: secundis rebus insolentiores,.— Sup.: insolentissimi homines, Cael. ad .—

Immoderately; haughtily, insolently: Gorgias his festivitatibus insolentius abutitur,: auctorem extinctum laete atque insolenter ferre,with insolent exultation,: victoriā suā insolenter gloriari,: se efferre,: a sorore irrisa,: dictum,: hostis insequens,.—Comp.: se insolentius jactare,; . — Sup.: insolentissime obequitare,.

la:verb:insum.gloss: to be in, to be on

la:verb:insum.html:
in-sum, fui, esse, v. n.,

la:verb:insisto.html:
in-sisto, stĭti, 3, v. n.,
to set foot upon, to stand, tread, or press upon; constr. mostly with dat., also with in and abl. or acc., or the simple acc. (class.).
Lit.
In gen.
With dat.: nec desunt villae quae secutae fluminis amoenitatem margini insistunt,: ut proximi jacentibus insisterent,stepped upon them,: alternis pedibus,: volucres metuunt insistere ramis,: vestigiis,: huic (saxo) institerat frustra,: plantis,: clamoso circo,occupy a place in,.—
With in and abl.: insistebat in manu Cereris dextra simulacrum Victoriae,: cingulus australis, in quo qui insistunt,: in jugo,: ipse non insistere in terra poterat,.—
With in and acc.: in sinistrum pedem,; cf.: corvus repente super galeam insistit,lights,.—
With the simple acc.: plantam,: limen,to step upon, to tread the threshold,: vestigia nuda sinistri pedis,: primis infans vestigia plantis,: cineres,.—
Esp.
To enter on or pursue a way, path, or journey: cum semel institerunt vestigia certa viaï,: huc an illuc iter,: omnes itinera insistant sua,: quam insistam viam,; ; .—
In hostile sense, to follow, pursue, press on; with dat.: effusis hostibus,: fugientibus,: contenti non institere cedentibus,; .—Pass. impers.: ut fracto jam Maroboduo, usque in exitium insisteretur,.—
Trop.
In gen., to follow, pursue.
With acc.: viam domandi,: rationem pugnae,plan,.—
With dat.: vestigiis laudum suarum,: honoribus,.—
Esp.
To follow up, pursue an object or enterprise; to press vigorously, apply one's self to: in dolos,: totus et mente et animo in bellum,. — With acc.: hoc negotium,: manus,.—With dat.: rebus magnis,: perdomandae Campaniae,.—
To set about, devote one's self to, to begin with zeal; with inf.: tribuni orare dictatorem insistunt, ut, etc., : Appium institit sequi,; ; ; cf.: postero die ad spolia legenda foedamque spectandam stragem insistunt,: flagitare senatus institit Coruntum, ut,. — Absol.: sic institit ore,i. e. began to speak,; cf.: sic insistit secumque corde volutat,i. e. to reflect, think,.—
To persevere, continue, persist in; with inf.: credere,: tueri,.—With dat.: sin crudelitati insisteret,: spei,: caedibus,: studiis,to pursue diligently,: obsidioni,: curae rerum,: funeri,to set forward,. — Absol.: importune,to persist,; .—
To press upon, urge; with dat.: atriensibus ut supellectilem exponant,: id bellum ipsis institit moenibus,was at,.—Absol.: dilataque tempora taedae Institerant,were at hand,: institit quantum potuit ut illum ex eorum manibus liberaret,urged, insisted,. —
To press upon, repress; and hence, to halt, pause, stop, stand still: stellarum motus insistunt,: ut non referat pedem, insistet certe,; : quae cum dixisset paulumque institisset,; : saepe accidit, ut aut citius insistendum sit, aut longius procedendum,; so, to pause in thought, hesitate, doubt: ille in reliquis rebus non poterit eodem modo insistere?; .—

la:verb:insido.html:
in-sīdo, sēdi (
perf. insidi, ), sessum, 3, v. n. and a., to sit down in or on, to settle on; constr. with dat. (poet. and post-Aug.).
Lit.
In gen.: apes floribus insidunt,: inscia Dido, Insidat quantus miserae deus,; volucres metuunt insidere ramis,. — With acc.: locum,: apex insiditur astris,: littera "i" sibi insidit, coniicit enim est ab illo jacit,coalesces,: digitos membris,sink into,.—

la:verb:insido.inflection: sēdi, sessum, 3, v. n. and a.

la:noun:insania.html:
insānĭa, ae, f.
insanus
,
unsoundness of mind.
As a disease, madness, insanity, sqq.—
As a personal quality, madness, frenzy, folly, senselessness: nomen insaniae significat mentis aegrotationem et morbum,: sanitatem animorum positam in tranquillitate quadam constantiaque censebant: his rebus mentem vacuam appellarunt insaniam,: furorem esse rati sunt, mentis ad omnia caecitatem: quod cum majus esse videatur, quam insania, tamen ejusmodi est, ut furor in sapientem cadere possit, non possit insania,: concupiscere aliquid ad insaniam,to madness,: favere alicui ad insaniam,: adigere ad insaniam,: scelerata belli,: quae tanta insania, cives?: nudus agas, minus est insania turpis,—
Plur.: hunc intem periae insaniaeque agitant senem,: incideram in hominum pugnandi cupidorum insanias,. —
Trop.
Madness, i. e. excess, extravagance in any thing: villarum,: libidinum,: ut appareret, quam ab sano initio res in hanc insaniam venerit, Liv 7, 2, 13: mensarum,.—
Of speech: orationis,.—
Poetic enthusiasm, rapture, inspiration: auditis? an me ludit amabilis Insania?.

la:verb:insono.gloss: to make a sound or noise in or on; sound, sound loudly, resound, roar
senses: to make a sound or noise in or on; sound, sound loudly, resound, roar
la:verb:insono.html:
in-sŏno, ŭi, 1, v. n.,
to make a noise in or on, to sound, sound loudly, resound (mostly poet.): Boreae cum spiritus alto Insonat Aegaeo,roars on the Ægean Sea,: insonuere cavernae,: caeli delapsa per auras Insonuit,resounded flying through the air,; cf. pennis,: calamis,to play upon,: insonuitque flagello,cracked his whip,; cf. poet. with acc.: verbera insonuit,: quasi faucibus aliquid obstiterit, insonare, to clear one's throat, to hawk, .

la:adj:insons.html:
in-sons, ntis, adj.
Guiltless, innocent; constr. with gen. or absol. (class., but not in Cic. or Cæs.): insontem probri accusare,: aliquem falso atque insontem arguere,: publici consilii,: culpae,.— With abl. (rare): si regni crimine insons fuerit,.—Absol.: purus et insons ... si vivo,; : amicus,; . — Esp., as subst.: insontes, um, m., the innocent (opp. sontes): circumvenire, jugulare,.—
Harmless (only poet.): Cerberus,: oliva,: casa,.

la:verb:insulto.gloss: to spring, leap or jump at or upon
senses: to spring, leap or jump at or upon
to revile, abuse, taunt or insult
la:verb:insulto.html:
insulto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
[insilio], to spring or leap at or upon a thing, to leap, bound, jump, spring.
Lit.: fores calcibus,: floribus,: sub armis Insultare solo,: busto,: fluctibus insultavere carinae,: Batavi dum insultant aquis,: rogis, (2, 8, b. 4. M.).—
With acc.: nemora avia matres Insultant thiasis,.—
Absol.: fremit aequore toto Insultans sonipes. .—
Trop., to behave insolently towards any one, to scoff at, revile, abuse, taunt, insult: alicui in calamitate,: dominis,: alicui per contumelias,: adversis rebus eorum,: jacenti,: casibus alicujus,.—
With acc.: multos bonos, ap. Don. ad ; : patientiam et segnitiam cujuspiam,.—
With in and acc.: in rem publicam,: in omnes,.—
With abl.: morte mea,at my death, (4, 5), 24.—(ε) Absol.: quippe impune se insultaturos,: cernis ut insultent Rutuli,exult,.
la:verb:insulto.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.

la:adj:insanus.html:
in-sānus, a, um, adj.,
unsound in mind.
Lit., mad, insane (syn.: furiosus, fanaticus): quod idem contigit insanis,: si fecisset Juno maritum insanum,. —
Transf., that acts like a madman, raging, raving, foolish, frantic.
Ex stultis insanos facere, : acrior et insanior cupiditas,: insanissima concio,: homo insanissimus,: uter est insanior horum?.—
Transf., of inanim. and abstr. things: caedis insana cupido,: amor duri Martis,: insano verba tonare foro,i. e. where there is a great bustle,omnis et insana semita nocte sonat,i. e. of women raving about,: insani enses,: fluctus,: venti,: vires Austri,: insana Caprae sidera,. —
That causes madness (cf. "The insane root, that takes the reason prisoner," Shaks. Macb. 1, 3): laurum insanam vocant, quoniam si quid ex ea decerptum inferatur navibus, jurgia fiunt, donec abiciatur,: herba,that produces madness,: fames,that drives one to madness,.—
Outrageous, monstrous, violent, extravagant, excessive: substructionum insanae moles,: substructiones Capitolii insanae,: labor,: trepidatio,: cum stupet insanis acies fulgoribus,: vites,that bear excessively, three times,; cf. adv., 3. insanum. —
Enthusiastic, enraptured, inspired: vates,. — Adv., in three forms.
insānē.
Madly, insanely: amare,. — Comp.: in silvam non ligna feras insanius,.—Sup.: insanissime desperare,.—
Outrageously, excessively: esuriens insane bene,; cf. Müll.—
in-sānĭter, madly, violently, excessively: ludit nimium insaniter, Pomp. ap. ; P.—
insānum, outrageously, vehemently, excessively: insanum malum = pessimum,: porticus, insanum bona,: magnum molior negotium,: valde, id. Fragm. ap. .

la:verb:insideo.gloss: to sit down, in or upon; to be seated or rest in or upon
senses: to sit down, in or upon; to be seated or rest in or upon
to be fixed or stamped in; adhere to
to be situated upon, stand upon, take place upon, occupy
to take possession of, hold, occupy
la:verb:insideo.html:
insĭdĕo, sēdi, sessum, 2, v. n. and a.
[in-sedeo], to sit in or upon any thing; mostly with dat. (class.).
Neutr.
Lit.: equo,: curru insidens,: solo,.—
To settle: ubi Lydia quondam jugis insedit Etruscis,.—
Trop., to be seated, fixed, or stamped in, to adhere to: cum in locis semen insedit,: longus morbus, cum penitus insedit,when it has become deeply seated,: insidens capulo manus,i. e. keeping firm hold of the handle,: nihil quisquam unquam, me audiente, egit orator, quod non in memoria mea penitus insederit,remained thoroughly fixed in my mind,: insidebat in ejus mente species eloquentiae,was firmly stamped on his mind,: voluptas, quae penitus in omni sensu implicata insidet,: cum hic fervor concitatioque animi inveteraverit, et tamquam in venis medullisque insederit,has firmly seated itself,.—
Act., to sit or be situated upon, stand upon, take place upon, occupy.
Lit.: currum,: Joppe insidet collem,. —
Transf., to take possession of a place, to hold, occupy: locum,: juga,: militibus arcem,: insidere vias examina infantium solebant,: Aventinum,; ; Dietsch: medium mare,: arcem Capitolii,: ea loca,inhabit,. — Pass.: viaeque omnes hostium praesidiis insidentur,: saltus circa insessus ab hoste,: per montes praesidiis nostris insessos,: insessus iterum Alpibus,: insessum diris avibus Capitolium,occupied as a perch,.
la:verb:insideo.inflection: sēdi, sessum, 2, v. n. and a.

la:verb:inserto.html:
inserto, 1,
v. a. freq. [id.], to put into, insert; with dat. (poet. and post - Aug.): clipeoque sinistram Insertabam aptans,: dextras catenis,: insertans commissuris secures,.

la:verb:insterno.html:
in-sterno, strāvi, strātum, 3, v. a.
To cover, cover over: instrata cubilia fronde,; so, instratos ostro,; cf.: si palo adacto caverna paleā insternatur,: pontes altos,.—
Transf., to lay upon as a cover, to spread over: modicis instravit pulpita tignis (dat.), laid the stage over an insignificant scaffolding, .—
To cast or throw into: sese Ignibus,.

senses: to repeat, start, or perform anew or afresh; renew (after a period of disuse), resume
la:verb:instauro.html:
in-stauro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
staurus, obs., = Gr. σταυρός, a paling, stake; cf. Sanscr. sthavaras, firm; root stare, ἵστημι
,
to renew, repeat, celebrate anew; to repair, restore; to erect, make (syn.: renovo, integro; class.): Latinas,: caedem, Auct. Or. pro Dom. 3: (with renovare) scelus pristinum,: novum de integro bellum,: infestis pugnam sagittis,: societatem.

: omne genus operis, auspicandi causa,: cinere aut gypso instaurare vina,: sibi monumenta,: opus,: sibi tunicas,: instaurati animi,refreshed,: sacrum diis loci,to offer, perform,: dī, talia Graiis, Instaurate,i. e. to repay, requite,: pervigiles popinas,to frequent anew,.

la:verb:insurgo.html:
in-surgo, surrexi, rectum, 3, v. n.
To rise upon, to rise up or to: insurgite remis, rise on your oars, i. e. ply your oars vigorously, ; ; ; so, remis insurgitur,: insurgit transtris,: nigro glomerari pulvere nubem Prospiciunt Teucri, ac tenebras insurgere campis,: sibilat insurgens capiti,raising its head,.—
With acc.: jugum (i. q. in jugum),.—
To raise one's self, to rise, mount: insurgat Aquilo,: si forte prolapsus est, attolli et insurgere haud licitum,: altior insurgens et cursu concitus heros,: et (serpens) sibilat ore, Arduus insurgens,: acuta silex Speluncae dorso insurgens,: inde colles insurgunt,: pone tergum insurgebat silva,; so in fight, to rise for a blow: ostendit dextram insurgens Entellus,: altior,. —
Transf.
To rise, grow in power: insurgere regnis alicujus, to rise against, i. e. to aim at seizing one's kingdom, : Caesar insurgere paulatim,: Romanas opes insurgere,. —
Of waters, floods: vastius insurgens decimae ruit impetus undae,: Atax usque eo solitus insurgere, ut se ipse non capiat, .—
To arise: insurgunt fremitus,. —
To rise up, to rouse or bestir one's self: invigilare publicis utilitatibus et insurgere,.—
Of speech, to rise above the level of ordinary language, to become sublime: Horatius insurgit aliquando,: augeri debent sententiae, et insurgere,: haec sunt, quibus mens pariter et oratio insurgant,; .

la:adj:insperatus.html:
in-spērātus, a, um, adj.,

inspērātē, unexpectedly, .—Comp.: insperatius,, ext. 2; . —
inspērātō, unexpectedly (anteand post-class.): illam augeam, Fleck.: abiit, Lucil. ap. : aulam invenit,: insperato et contra opinionem,.

la:adj:insomnis.html:
in-somnis, e, adj.
2. in-somnus
,
sleepless (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Of living beings, : juventus,: insomnes magis, quam pervigiles,: draco,.—
Of things: oculi,: dens,i. e. of the dragon, from which armed men sprung,: nox,: cura,.

insomnĭa, ae, f. (plur.insomnia, n., ; ; ; ; ) [insomnis],

la:verb:instigo.gloss: to stimulate, set on, incite, rouse or urge

la:verb:instigo.html:
instīgo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
from in and stigo (unused), cf. Gr. στίζω; Sanscr. tig, tij, to be sharp; cf. stimulus for stig-mulus, stilus for stig-lus
,

la:adj:insuetus.html:
in-suētus, a, um, adj.,

Not accustomed to, unused to a thing; constr. with gen., dat., ad, or inf.
With gen.: insuetus contumeliae,: laboris,: hujus generis pugnae,: navigandi,: operum,: male audiendi,: moris ejus insueta,; : libertatis, Dietsch.—

la:adj:inspoliatus.html:
in-spŏlĭātus, a, um, adj.,
not plundered (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): occi sus est non praedae gratiā, quia inspoliatus est,; : arma,.

in-sĭpĭens (insăp-, Schol. Bob. ad ; p. 304, 16 Bait.), entis, adj.

inspectĭo, ōnis, f.

inspicio

la:verb:insero.html:
in-sĕro, sēvi, sĭtum, 3, v. a.
in-, 1. sero
,
to sow or plant in; to ingraft (class.).
Lit.: frumentum,: pirum bonam in pirum silvaticam,to ingraft, graft,: vitem,: fissā modo cortice virgam Inserit,; : inseritur et nucis arbutus horrida fetu, Forbig. ad loc.; so, cum Vergilius insitam nucibus arbutum dicat,. —

la:adj:insolitus.html:
in-sŏlĭtus, a, um, adj.,

in-sĕpultus, a, um, adj.

,
